name: Multi-agent systems
summary: Several agents with different roles or contexts work together on one task.

text: Big jobs are easier with a team: one person plans, others do the parts, and someone checks the work.
Multi-agent systems are teams of AIs.
D1.analogy: A team with a planner, workers and a checker.

text: An **orchestrator** agent splits a task and hands pieces to **sub-agents**, each with its own instructions and context window.
Sub-agents return summaries rather than everything they saw, which keeps the orchestrator's context focused.
Benefits: parallel work and separation of concerns. Costs: more tokens, coordination errors and harder debugging.
D2.analogy: A team with a planner, workers and a checker.
D2.analogyBreaks: Human teammates share background knowledge. Sub-agents share nothing except what's written in their instructions, so vague hand-offs fail silently.

predict.question: Why might an orchestrator give each sub-agent a fresh context?
options: So each can focus on its piece without filling up the orchestrator's context
predict.explanation: Separate contexts keep each agent focused and return only conclusions to the lead agent.

text: Open problems: when multi-agent setups beat one strong agent, communication protocols between agents (such as A2A), and agents amplifying each other's mistakes.

sources.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
